Codex CLI configuration contract, MEASURED — not read from documentation.

  codex-cli 0.147.0 · macos-aarch64 · captured 2026-08-26

This file exists because a code review asserted a different contract than the
one the installed CLI implements, and prose could not settle it. Everything
below is either verbatim CLI output or the resolved-model readout of a
purpose-built fixture. hardening_round8_test.go asserts the observer's
implemented precedence against these bytes.


1. PROFILE SELECTION — verbatim from `codex --help`
---------------------------------------------------

  -p, --profile <CONFIG_PROFILE_V2>
          Layer $CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml on top of the base user config

Two things this settles:

  * `-p` is the short alias for `--profile`; both select the same thing.
  * The selection is an OVERLAY FILE, $CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml — not a
    [profiles.<name>] table inside config.toml. The value type is literally
    named CONFIG_PROFILE_V2 because the table is the V1 shape it replaced.

Reading the legacy table for a current run is the unsafe direction: a stale
[profiles.unsafe] table saying sandbox_mode = "read-only" would be signed for
a run whose selected unsafe.config.toml granted danger-full-access.


2. BASE USER CONFIGURATION — verbatim from `codex --help`
---------------------------------------------------------

  -c, --config <key=value>
          Override a configuration value that would otherwise be loaded from
          `~/.codex/config.toml`.

$CODEX_HOME/config.toml (default ~/.codex/config.toml) is the base layer.


3. PROJECT CONFIGURATION — measured, `codex doctor` model readout
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Method: write a distinctive `model` into one candidate location at a time,
run `codex doctor` from a working directory inside a git repository, and read
back the "model" line of its Configuration section. The user config's model is
gpt-5.6-sol, so any other value proves the candidate was loaded.

  candidate location                     cwd            resolved model
  -------------------------------------  -------------  --------------------
  <cwd>/.codex/config.toml               <repo>/zzprobe cwd-dotcodex-model
  <repo-root>/.codex/config.toml         <repo>/zzprobe project-layer-model
  <cwd>/config.toml                      <repo>/zzprobe gpt-5.6-sol  (IGNORED)
  <repo-root>/config.toml                <repo>/zzprobe gpt-5.6-sol  (IGNORED)

Conclusion: the project tier is `.codex/config.toml` in each directory from
the working directory up to the project root. A BARE `config.toml` is not a
Codex configuration file at any level.

That distinction is load-bearing for this attestor. A bare config.toml is an
ordinary repository file in many ecosystems; treating one as Codex project
configuration both digested an unrelated file into signed evidence as Codex
configuration and suppressed resolution of the user tier that did describe
the run.
